label: retired id allowed back: the ledger never reports a retired id the catalog uses again (.retiredNeverReused)
an id dropped from the catalog reads as kept, so removing one without retiring it passes (.removedIsRetired)
the undo law compares history only, not bytes, so an undo that keeps the change passes (.undoRestoresBytes)
the step-name law reads the title, not the history, so a misnamed step passes (.stepNamedTitle)
the history exemption covers every view and query, so a view or query that writes bytes passes (.queryOrViewChangesNoBytes)
an example that fails its schema still counts as conforming when its run is skipped (.exampleValidates)
find: return problems + [CatalogLaw.exampleValidates.problem(id, "the example fails its params schema: \(why)")]
